newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds dip, spreads narrow after FOMC.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds dip, spreads narrow after FOMC.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities gyrated most of the day, ending on the downside after the Federal Reserve ratcheted up short-term interest rates by a quarter-point on Tuesday.
Pass-through yield spreads narrowed by a few ticks over Treasuries, and trading volume was heavy late in the session, traders said.
Late Tuesday, mortgages were unchanged to 8/32 lower overall, while comparable Treasuries were off 11/32 to 13/32.
"Yield spreads have been bouncing around with Treasuries most of the day," one mortgage trader said, adding that spreads were slightly tighter by late afternoon.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were off 7/32 at 98-23/32 bid, yielding 104 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was down 7/32 at 98-27/32 bid, while Freddie Mac issues were 8/32 lower at 99 even bid.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 13/32 at 96-11/32 bid, to yield 6.76 percent.
